chapter: Move to New York and the Stuyvesant
title: Hearing the second Stuyvesant band with Don Ewell
summary: Blumberg dates his move to after the second Stuyvesant engagement and recalls Don's Jelly Roll style piano and Bunk taking more solos; Maude's presence is mentioned.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yeah, well, of course, when I moved up to New York, I think the Stuyvesant engagement was over already. That ended about the 10th or so. Well, this was the second.
I didn't move up, I think, until after the second one was over. The second one, when Don was there.

Yeah. Did you get up to hear the band with Don? Oh, yeah, I came up to hear the band with Don, and that was very exciting, too, because Don was playing exceptionally well with the band, and Kratka and I and a few others used to stand behind the piano there and just listen to the piano, which was very exciting, some very exciting Jelly Roll style.
Yeah, Don was playing more Jelly Roll style then than he does now.

Yeah. Yeah. And Bunk was very pleased with Don. He used to get up and walk around and stand beside the piano and play a solo, which before that he had never made very much of a point of playing solos, I don't think. I mean, he had certain solos he'd do in certain numbers, but he'd just stand up and do them. He really tried to do a little more with setting off his solos as apart from the ensembles. When Don was with the band, he'd go over and stand next to the piano and do a real solo type solo and very pretty things. You didn't move up then? I didn't move up until after that was over.

That second engagement, if I remember rightly, was the only one when Maude was up there, too. There was something you were telling the other night, the time when Maude was at the table. I forget what the story is now, but you were there once when she was there in New York, too.
